issuer: the Royal Falkland Islands Police Licensing Bureau (its licensing services run through the Post Office)
note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Royal Falkland Islands Police's own pages (gov.fk/police). Its Driving Licence Application Form C (dated 20 February 2020, uploaded in January 2026; read from its text, saved as fk-formC.txt): a driver's licence for class A, B, BA or B1 is applied for by someone at least 17 who has passed the written and practical tests (class A alone from 16), so the full licence is held from 17. The form gives the fee as £30.90, but the Driving Licences page today charges £31.80 for exchanging a foreign licence where the form charges £30.90 for the same, so the form's fee is out of date and the fee for a licence after the tests isn't known: null. The page says an exchanged licence is valid permanently, but gives no term for one issued after the tests, so the term is null. No exchange list is held (any valid foreign licence is exchanged within 12 months, on the form's proofs; holding every country isn't a list the page gives). No identity card is held.

sources.title: Royal Falkland Islands Police, Driving Licence Application Form C (20.02.2020), text of the .docx
sources.said: I am at least 17 years of age and applying for a driver’s licence to drive a *class A, *class B, *class BA, *class B1 motor vehicle. ... I have passed the written and practical tests of competency and enclose the test pass certificates. ... I enclose the fee of £30.90.

sources.title: Royal Falkland Islands Police Licensing Bureau, Driving Licences
sources.said: LICENSING SERVICES ARE MANAGED BY THE POST OFFICE. ... All foreign driving licences must be exchanged to Falkland Islands driving licence within the cumulative 12 month period. The fee for this is £31.80 GBP and is valid permanently from date of issue.
